questions.question:
Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s).

Statements: Some papers are pens.

All the pencils are pens.

Conclusions (I): Some pens are pencils.

Conclusions (II): Some pens are papers.
questions.solution:
The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f9eba63fe547d740f5a29054d055326a6bd059c3912adf91ca0adac94cd67779.png] 

**Conclusions:**

(I): Some pens are pencils → **True **(As, All the pencils are pens. so, Some pens are pencils holds true).

(II): Some pens are papers → **True **(As, Some papers are pens. so, Some pens are papers holds true)

Thus, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

questions.question:
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.

12, 16, 22, 32, ?
questions.solution:
**The logic followed here is:**

The given number series is: 12, 16, 22, 32, ?

 
 

 12
 →
 16

 →
 32
 →
 46

 +6
 
 +10

Now, let's analyze the pattern in the sequence of these increments: 4, 6, 10.

 

 
 
 
 

 Increment
 Pattern Derived
 
 

 4
 2 × 2 (2 is the 1st prime number)
 
 

 6
 2 × 3 (3 is the 2nd prime number)
 
 

 10

The pattern shows that each increment is obtained by multiplying 2 by consecutive prime numbers (starting from 2).

The next prime number after 5 is 7.

Next Increment = 2 × 7 = 14

Missing Term = 32 + 14 = 46

Thus, the missing term in the series is **46**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**;

questions.question:
What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if '+' and '−' are interchanged and '×' and '÷' are interchanged?

22 × 484 ÷ 44 − 93 + 12 = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule:

 [IMAGE: https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/c0j5U9v2oJWEzSTKvdDLWZ5Zik3PBUXk-C9w3Ma990WH63rpQUfA7g-3wh_uT7CgFvFJ4jPGEeOw509FxSgfh78_HR9tDNZ9KitXdEveKsLaLMgPQf6YSDt1b775728JMVp9FIQs=s0] 

Given the interchange rules: 

__
 
• ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged. 
 
• ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged.

Now,

Given e×pression: 22 × 484 ÷ 44 − 93 + 12

After replacing the symbols.

⇒ 22 ÷ 484 × 44 + 93 − 12

Perform operations according to BODMAS:

⇒ **22 ÷ 484**__ × 44 + 93 − 12

⇒ (1/22) × 44 + 93 − 12

⇒ __**(1 × 44) / 22**__ + 93 − 12

⇒ __**2 + 93**__ − 12

⇒ __**95 − 12**__

⇒ 83

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

After replacing the symbols with their meanings:

⇒ 41 × 6 − 99 ÷ 3 + 9

Perform operations according to BODMAS:

⇒ **41 × 6**__ − __**99 ÷ 3**__ + 9

⇒ 246 − 33 + 9

⇒ __**246 - 33**__ + 9

⇒ __**213 + 9**__

⇒ 222

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3".

questions.question:
Six persons P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6 sit around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). P2 sits second to the left of P5. One person sits between P2 and P6 when counted from the left of P2. P3 and P2 are not neighbours of P5 and P4, respectively.

Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

I. One person sits between P1 and P6 when counted from the right of P1.

II. P3 is an immediate neighbour of P2.
questions.solution:
Given:

Six persons P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 and P6 sit around a circular table facing towards the centre.

P2 sits second to the left of P5.

One person sits between P2 and P6 when counted from the left of P2.

P3 and P2 are not neighbours of P5 and P4, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8d065a7987ef7ba914748f6893ec96fc7dc5a72c7708a0f70d92c80898fd3f3d.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd256df1da174b6df4a317b58d8d4db874954e18fdb78d371ad50c9614377afb.png] 

I. One person sits between P1 and P6 when counted from the right of P1 is **wrong **statement as, 2 person sits between P1 and P6.

II. P3 is an immediate neighbour of P2, which is a correct statement.

Thus, Only II statement is correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**
